title: Pay stubs and tax records tied two San Francisco workplaces to one wage case

beats.text: A factory complaint reached San Francisco investigators in 2008.

visual.sub: A complaint led from a frozen-food factory to a retail market

beats.text: They traced another workplace to a market on Clement Street.

visual.kicker: A complaint led from a frozen-food factory to a retail market

beats.text: The factory’s pay stubs printed $8.50 an hour.

visual.label: Handwritten marks told a different story from the printed hourly rate

beats.text: Workers described earning $7, partly in cash. Investigators credited that cash.

visual.kicker: Handwritten marks told a different story from the printed hourly rate

beats.text: One week after a site visit, a request was filed to change the factory’s tax registration.

visual.kicker: City records linked two businesses the owners said were separate

beats.text: A June 2008 filing listed a different corporation as owner.

visual.kicker: City records linked two businesses the owners said were separate

beats.text: The factory sold in 2011. The officer found none of the proceeds went to back wages.

visual.kicker: The factory changed hands while the workers waited

beats.text: The officer awarded back wages and interest to 35 workers.

visual.label: The final decision separated back wages, interest and two equal penalties

beats.text: Two equal penalties followed. One was owed to workers and one to the City.
The decision establishes the award. What workers actually received remains an open question.

visual.kicker: The final decision separated back wages, interest and two equal penalties
